clue.text: Money split by drummer and guitarist initially sharing top billing

indicators.note: the word for money is broken open so that the drummer's name sits in its middle

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money
Ringo Starr, the Beatles' drummer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of guitarist is wanted

parts.note: G is the first letter of guitarist

explanation.surface: A band's money is shared between drummer and guitarist, who both get equal billing.
explanation.walkthrough: The drummer is Ringo STARR of the Beatles; the coin is opened up around him, then the guitarist's G closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who co-star share equal prominence in a film's credits, so co-starring means sharing top billing.

clue.text: Market slump wiping out the last of broker's money

indicators.note: the letter is removed entirely from the word for a slump

parts.note: a crash is a sudden collapse in market prices
the final letter of the word broker, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A stock market collapse wipes out a broker's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is money in the form of notes and coins.

clue.text: Prominent boxer interrupting broadcast

indicators.note: the boxer cuts into the middle of the word for broadcast

parts.note: a message broadcast is sent out
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: A prominent boxer interrupts a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is the most noticeable or important one, so it stands out.

clue.text: Extra exhaust put in and modified

indicators.note: once combined, the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: to do someone is British slang for wearing them out, as in done in
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extra car exhaust gets fitted and modified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' suggests a car part, but it is the verb: to tire out, as in 'done'.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item or feature attached to something else.

clue.text: Places that are haunted, or covered in spiders?

indicators.note: the word or is wrapped inside the snooker word

parts.note: in snooker a spider is a type of rest, a stand for the cue
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spooky haunted places, or ones crawling with spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunted' suggests ghosts, but it means frequented: people haunt their favourite resorts. In snooker, a spider is a raised rest for the cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place people visit often, and to haunt somewhere is to frequent it.

clue.text: County fair ultimately taken in by nary a soul?

indicators.note: the letter is absorbed into the phrase for nobody

parts.note: no folk means nobody at all

indicators.note: the last letter of fair is the one wanted

parts.note: R is the last letter of fair

explanation.surface: A county fair that, in the end, attracts nobody at all.
explanation.walkthrough: NORFOLK is a rural county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is one of the counties of England, on its east coast.

clue.text: Verbally, gents perhaps take a beating

indicators.note: spoken out, the plural for toilets gives the same sound as the answer

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, one example of loos

explanation.surface: Someone in a public toilet is said to be taking a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is the British name for a men's public toilet; loo is everyday British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose a contest is to be defeated, which is the idiomatic sense of taking a beating.

clue.text: Gold coin tossed over river

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: a tossed coin is flung about, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the four letters of coin, rearranged
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A gold coin is tossed across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major river of South America, flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Provoked strange need to have sex inside?

indicators.note: the word for sex goes within the jumbled letters
the letters of need are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of need, rearranged
gender is a person's sex

explanation.surface: A strange need to have sex provoked something.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender a feeling is to cause or give rise to it, so engendered means caused or brought about.

clue.text: Husband has antagonism towards dependant

parts.note: anger is hostility or antagonism
on can mean towards, as in to march on a city

explanation.surface: A husband resents someone who depends on him.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a person who attaches themselves to another for benefit, a parasitic follower.

clue.text: Sadly rejected, daughter leaves

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly or unfortunately

explanation.surface: A daughter, rejected, sadly leaves home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb about the daughter departing, but it is the definition as a noun: salad greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a dish made of green leaves such as lettuce, so leaves is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Each male appearing in series being shown online

indicators.note: the two short pieces show up inside the word for a series

parts.note: a string is a series of things, as in a string of wins

explanation.surface: Every man appears in a TV series that is now available online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series' suggests a TV show, which suits the surface, but here it means a string of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaming is the delivery of video or audio over the internet as it plays, so it is shown online.

clue.text: Painter's sign crossing over a road

indicators.note: the star sign straddles the other pieces, its letters on either side of them

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
on can mean over, as in a lid on a box
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's sign stretches across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; LEO splits into LE...O around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, known simply by his first name.

clue.text: Both sides of glacier have increased in size

indicators.note: only the two end letters of glacier, its first and last, are used

parts.note: G and R are the outermost letters of glacier
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Both edges of a glacier have got bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown is the past participle of grow, and having grown is having become larger.

clue.text: Literary assistant a guy uses in … in error

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a guy

indicators.note: something in error is wrong, so these letters are set out in a mistaken order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary assistant is a man who misuses words.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the two halves, so the first 'in' is fodder and the second begins the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a person who takes dictation or copies manuscripts, a writer's secretary.

clue.text: Flash couples embracing the core of activist's causes

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash of time

indicators.note: the word for couples holds the central letter in its arms

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join, so ties are couples
the central letter of activist, the V among its middle pair

explanation.surface: In a moment, linked pairs take up the heart of an activist's causes.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the reasons behind actions, the things that cause a person to act.

clue.text: Nobleman set about restraining unruly cousin

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the jumble between them
turned about, the letters for a television set run backwards

parts.note: a TV is a television set

indicators.note: an unruly cousin is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters of cousin, rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman sets about controlling his unruly cousin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' reads as 'began', but 'set' is a TV set and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British peer ranking between an earl and a baron.

clue.text: At first, kids are bored by perfectly fine musical entertainment

indicators.note: only the leading letter of kids is taken

parts.note: K is the first letter of kids

indicators.note: the word are is pierced, with the other piece drilled into its middle

parts.note: taken as written
A-OK means perfectly all right

explanation.surface: Children start out bored, even though everything is perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is a pastime of singing along to recorded backing tracks, a form of musical fun.

clue.text: Function held in Northern Ireland returned excellent capital

indicators.note: the trig function is gripped between the other letters
sent back, so the excellent grade is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
cos is the cosine, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A function is held in Northern Ireland and comes back an excellent success.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is treated as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Presided over cleaners, primarily with a mop?

indicators.note: in first place, so only the opening letter of cleaners

parts.note: C is the first letter of cleaners
a mop is a thick head of hair, so having one is being haired

explanation.surface: Someone presided over the cleaners, mostly armed with a mop.
explanation.walkthrough: The mop is not a cleaning tool here but a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it as its leader.

clue.text: Cunning, extremely deliberate, firm style of design

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning, as in artful

indicators.note: at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of deliberate

parts.note: D and E are the outer letters of deliberate
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A cunning, deliberate firm adopts a style of design.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, with bold geometric forms.

clue.text: Cheat on exclusive gaming device

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
sole means exclusive, as in sole rights

explanation.surface: Someone cheats on an exclusive games machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A console is a home video-game machine such as a PlayStation or Xbox.

clue.text: Squash my face

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their face has been squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash here is the British fruit drink made from concentrate, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain cordial and squash are both names for a sweet fruit concentrate diluted with water.

clue.text: Excessively wolfed down eggs — almost nine, by the sound of it

indicators.note: said aloud, the two pieces give the answer's pronunciation

parts.note: ova is the plural of ovum, an egg, and eight falls just one short of nine

explanation.surface: Someone greedily wolfed down nearly nine eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more than is good for you, so it fits gobbling food too much.

clue.text: Weary author occasionally lacking inspiration

indicators.note: only every other letter appears, as something happens now and then

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words spell the answer

explanation.surface: A tired writer sometimes has no inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking inspiration' reads as one phrase, but 'lacking' is just a link and 'inspiration' alone is the definition, the muse an author lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and a muse is a source of creative inspiration.

clue.text: Cow that circles about, having been oddly ignored

indicators.note: the word that wraps around the short piece

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping the second and fourth

parts.note: keeping the second and fourth letters of been leaves E and N

explanation.surface: A cow walks in circles, ignoring things now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is not the animal but the verb: to cow someone is to intimidate them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow is to frighten into submission, which is what one does by menacing or intimidating someone.

clue.text: Crime sees religious minister lose head

indicators.note: the word drops its opening letter, its head

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A crime sees a minister of religion lose his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Somewhat reckless plan to climb mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
only some of the letters, which sit inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of reckless and the start of plan

explanation.surface: A rather reckless plan to climb some mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: National park established around fantastically green island

indicators.note: the word for established surrounds the rearranged colour

parts.note: set means fixed or established

indicators.note: the letters of green are reworked into a wild new order

parts.note: the five letters of green, rearranged

explanation.surface: A national park was founded on a remarkably green island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti in Tanzania is a famous national park known for its wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Way to get everybody to stop running

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A way to get everyone to stop running around.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that stalls cuts out, ceasing to run.

clue.text: Drink in the end creates flipping trouble

indicators.note: only the final letter of creates is taken

parts.note: S is the final letter of creates

indicators.note: flipped over, the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in without further ado

explanation.surface: Drink ends up causing flipping trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink or carbonated water.

clue.text: Dutch keeper's covering ground, saving the day

indicators.note: the keeper's word goes over the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a holder is a keeper; holder's gives the plural-looking HOLDERS

indicators.note: saving means except, so the day is left out of the ground

parts.note: land is ground
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A Dutch goalkeeper covers the ground and saves the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as a goalkeeper's save but means 'except'. 'Dutch' is the noun, the people of Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollanders are people from Holland, that is the Dutch as a nation.
